newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Vox plans to remain independent of RTL.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Vox plans to remain independent of RTL.

text.p: German television broadcaster Vox has no plans to become more integrated in the RTL group if that means centralising planning and marketing, Vox president Markus Tellenbach told Reuters on Monday.

Tellenbach was responding to a report in the weekly news magazine Der Spiegel that French media group Canal Plus planned to sell its 24.9 percent stake in Vox to CLT/Ufa, Europe's largest broadcaster jointly owned by Bertelsmann and Audiofina.

Bertelsmann wants to take advantage of cost savings in marketing and advertising sales by linking its German television stations in a network, but the idea has run into opposition from shareholders of some of the smaller stations.
CLT/Ufa holds a large majority in RTL and controls 24.9 percent of Vox. The addition of the Canal Plus stake would give it nearly as much of Vox as Rupert Murdoch's News Corp holds.
Tellenbach said Canal Plus has not decided what to do with its Vox stake, and that it had not reached an agreement with CLT-Ufa, contrary to the Spiegel report.
"We do know, however, that in the medium term, Canal Plus wants to concentrate on the pay-TV business," he said.
Vox plans to remain an independent station offering a full range of programming with a focus on news and documentaries, Tellenbach said.
Both CLT-Ufa and News Corp are satisfied with Vox, whose business is developing "slowly but solidly", he said.
Vox hopes to turn a profit in 1998, after posting a 1997 loss in the double-digit millions of marks, he said.
